samples.summary: Namespace invoked with no subcommand (`wafflebase docs`, `wafflebase sheets`, `wafflebase ctx`, …) still bypasses the JSON envelope: it exits through `commander.help`, so it prints prose usage to stderr with exit 1 and no `USAGE` body
samples.evidence: `HELP_CODES` swallows `commander.help`. Commander v13's `_parseCommand` calls `this.help({ error: true })` for a command that has subcommands, no action handler and no operands — that is exactly `packages/cli/src/commands/sheets.ts:8` (`.command('sheets')` with only child commands, no `.action`), and likewise docs/notes/slides/files/api-keys/ctx/tabs/cells. That path emits code `commander.help` with exitCode 1, so `runCli` returns at cli.ts:83 having written only human prose to stderr. From an agent driver's point of view `wafflebase sheets get` (unknown command) now returns `{"error":{"code":"USAGE"}}` while `wafflebase sheets` — the same class of "you called me wrong" mistake, and the one a driver hits when it truncates a command — still returns unparseable prose. The new tests only cover bare `wafflebase`, not the namespace case.
searchedFor: grep '.command(' across packages/cli/src to find namespace commands without .action
read new tests in packages/cli/test/output.test.ts:404-498 (only bare `wafflebase` covered)

samples.summary: The `e instanceof CommanderError` branch will also swallow commander's `InvalidArgumentError` (a CommanderError subclass) if it ever escapes an action handler, relabelling a domain validation error as `USAGE` and stripping its prefix
samples.evidence: `InvalidArgumentError extends CommanderError` in commander. Any future custom `argParser`/action that throws one and lets it propagate is reported with code `USAGE` and a message mangled by `.replace(/^error: /, '')`, rather than its own code. No such throw exists in packages/cli today (grep for `InvalidArgumentError` in packages/cli returned nothing), so this is latent rather than firing now; a narrower check on `e.code.startsWith('commander.')` plus an explicit allow-list would close it.

samples.summary: `if (e.exitCode !== 0) process.exitCode = e.exitCode` never clears a previously-set failure code on the help/version path
samples.evidence: For `commander.help`/`commander.version` with exitCode 0 the code leaves `process.exitCode` at whatever it was. In the shipped `bin.ts` a single `runCli()` runs per process so nothing sets it earlier, but it also means commander's own `help()` (which computes its exit code as `Number(process.exitCode ?? 0)`) and this branch both inherit ambient state rather than deciding it — fine today, fragile if `runCli` is ever called twice in one process (as the tests already do, relying on an explicit `process.exitCode = 0` in `beforeEach`).
